papers.title_in_file: Cyc is a revolutionary AI platform with human reasoning, knowledge, and logic at enterprise scale: Technology Overview
papers.what_it_is: A Cycorp marketing and technology overview of the Cyc symbolic AI platform (knowledge base, CycL, inference engines, data integration, applications), written by the vendor with no experiments.

assertions.value: The authors state that the Cyc Knowledge Base comprises an ontology of about 1.5 million general concepts and more than 25 million general rules and assertions involving those concepts.
quotes: An ontology of about 1.5 million general concepts
More than 25 million general rules and assertions involving those concepts
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor's description of its own product; no independent count is given.
assertions.reader_inference: The earlier overview text (Section 2) says tens of millions of rules; the two figures are compatible but not identical.

assertions.value: The authors state that the Cyc Knowledge Base was built over the last 35 years with 2000+ Ph.D. scientist-years of effort, and describe the resulting effort as a quarter-billion-dollar investment.
quotes: Built over the course of the last 35 years, by 2000+ Ph.D. scientist-years’ eﬀort
As a result of our quarter-billion-dollar “pump-priming” and “infrastructure-building” eﬀort
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor's description of its own product history.

assertions.value: The authors claim that the Cyc Knowledge Base is the broadest, deepest, most complete AI tool ever developed.
quotes: is the broadest, deepest, most complete AI tool ever developed
assertions.certainty_reason: A superlative self-claim with no comparison or measurement in the paper.
assertions.reader_inference: No benchmark or comparison supports the superlative.

assertions.value: The authors state that Machine Learning harnesses big data to do statistical reasoning, whereas Cyc harnesses knowledge to do causal reasoning.
quotes: ML harnesses big data to do statistical reasoning, whereas Cyc harnesses knowledge to do causal reasoning.
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor's characterisation of its own product against a competing paradigm.

assertions.value: The authors state that machine learning identifies correlation, not causation, requires a large volume of training data, and cannot explain its results.
quotes: it identiﬁes correlation, not causation; it requires a large volume of training data; and it can’t explain its results.
assertions.certainty_reason: An unsupported general statement by a vendor whose product competes with ML.
assertions.reader_inference: The statement is stated without citation or evidence and is contradicted in part by the active field of ML explainability; it is not a settled fact.

assertions.value: The authors claim that ML can never give an explicit step-by-step explanation of its line of reasoning behind a conclusion, but that Cyc always can.
quotes: ML can never give an explicit step-by-step explanation of its line of reasoning behind a conclusion, but Cyc always can.
assertions.certainty_reason: A universal claim with no evidence in the paper.
assertions.reader_inference: Universal words (never, always) are not supported by any test in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors claim that leaders within large enterprises in the healthcare, financial services and energy industries trust Cyc in applications where their existing investments in ML and data science did not suffice, and that Cyc has delivered value in hundreds of deployments for commercial clients and government agencies.
quotes: trust Cyc in applications where their existing investments in ML and data science did not suﬃce
has delivered value in hundreds of deployments for commercial clients and government agencies
assertions.certainty_reason: Customer outcomes are asserted by the vendor; no named evaluation is given.

assertions.value: The authors claim that more than half of the largest 15 companies in the world, and their employees, have relied on Cyc applications to address their most critical issues.
quotes: More than half of the largest 15 companies in the world, and their employees, have relied on Cyc applications
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor's unverifiable customer claim; no companies are named.

assertions.value: The authors state that AI researchers have been developing knowledge-based systems capable of performing multistep logical reasoning since the early 1970s, and that perceptrons and expert systems each stalled for several decades; they attribute the revival to computing and memory cost and speed improving by more than a factor of 100,000 each since 1970.
quotes: have been developing knowledge-based systems capable of performing multistep logical reasoning since the early 1970s
more than a factor of 100,000 each—since 1970
assertions.certainty_reason: Historical summary stated without citation.

assertions.value: The authors state that there were 150 additional bottlenecks and missing technologies for expert systems back in 1970, besides the need for far faster and cheaper computers and storage, and that Cyc's engineers solved three typical ones (reusability, efficiency, inconsistency) and later others, in all 147 more breakthroughs.
quotes: there were actually 150 additional bottlenecks and missing technologies back in 1970
the other 147 breakthroughs required
assertions.certainty_reason: The figure 150 is a vendor's rhetorical count; no list of the 150 is given.
assertions.reader_inference: Only six of the 150 are named in the text, so the count cannot be checked from this paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that to remedy the non-reusability of expert system rules, Cycorp had to identify, collect and formalize the tens of millions of general rules of good guessing and good judgement that comprise general human common sense.
quotes: we had to identify, collect, and formalize the tens of millions of general rules of good guessing
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor's description of its own design rationale.

assertions.value: The authors state that Cyc implements over 1,000 special-case reasoners, each with its own data structures and algorithms, which work cooperatively as a community of agents in place of a general theorem prover; some are domain-dependent and some general, such as caching transitive relations.
quotes: we identiﬁed and implemented over 1,000 special-case reasoners
These work together cooperatively as a sort of community of agents to usurp the need for a general (but hopelessly slow) theorem prover.
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor's description of its own architecture.
assertions.reader_inference: Section 4 and Section 6.1 give over 1,100; the figure differs by about 100 between sections.

assertions.value: The authors state that the Cyc Inference Engines are a battery of over 1,100 inference engines that inter-operate as a community of agents, some general (such as efficient graph walks) and some domain-specific, and that over 1,100 redundant representations of assertions exist.
quotes: A battery of over 1,100 inference engines which inter-operate as a community of agents
In fact there are over 1,100 redundant representations, not just one
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor's description of its own architecture.

assertions.value: The authors state that Cyc replaces the requirement of global consistency of the knowledge base with local consistency, by situating each axiom in a microtheory (an explicitly represented logical context); axioms within one microtheory must be consistent, but need not be consistent with those in other microtheories.
quotes: we had to replace the requirement of global consistency of the knowledge base with the notion of local consistency.
Axioms within a single microtheory must be consistent with one another, but need not be consistent with those in other microtheories.
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor's description of its own design.

assertions.value: The authors state that microtheories are first class objects in Cyc's ontology, so Cyc can reason about them as it reasons about anything else in its knowledge base, and that this enables the meta-level reasoning about arguments.
quotes: is a ﬁrst class object in Cyc’s ontology, and can be reasoned about by Cyc;
it can reason about them just as it reasons about anything else in its knowledge base
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor's description of its own design.

assertions.value: The authors state that Cyc's inference engine keeps all pro and con arguments for an assertion, each consisting of justification chains, and decides by argumentation which arguments are preferred; incommensurable strong pro and con arguments make Cyc trust neither the statement nor its negation.
quotes: Whenever Cyc needs to decide something, it carries out a decision-making process called argumentation
result in Cyc deciding not to trust that statement or its negation, which is the right course of action.
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor's description of its own inference method.

assertions.value: The authors state that each assertion in Cyc has one or more justifications, bottoming out in what was told to be true in context C by source X at time Y.
quotes: Each assertion in Cyc has one or more justiﬁcations
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor's description of its own provenance model.
assertions.reader_inference: This is the same provenance idea as the Evidence Based DB's rule that every assertion names its source; the paper gives it as a design statement, not a tested feature.

assertions.value: The authors claim that CycL is 100% as expressive as natural languages such as English, and that anything that can be said in any natural language can also be said in CycL in full; they describe it as full higher order logic (HOL) and more expressive than triple-based languages such as OWL or RDF.
assertions.anchor: Section 4 item 1, p.5; Section 5.1, p.9; Section 5.2, p.9
quotes: CycL”, which is 100% as expressive as natural languages such as English
CycL is full HOL (higher order logic)
anything at all that anyone can say in any natural language can also be said in CycL in full
assertions.certainty_reason: An unproved universal expressiveness claim by the vendor.
assertions.reader_inference: No formal argument for the claim is given in the paper; a language that expresses all of natural language is an open claim.

assertions.value: The authors state that CycL, unlike OWL and knowledge graphs, allows relations to have any number of arguments, and give a 7-arity declaration of a fluid-flow principle as an example.
quotes: CycL allows relations to have any number of arguments.
This is a 7-arity declaration of a principle
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor's description of its own language; the example is given in the text.

assertions.value: The authors state that a knowledge graph consists only of triples that are binary relations between entities, that knowledge graphs require global consistency within a namespace, and that Cyc by contrast allows global inconsistency and requires local consistency only within microtheories.
quotes: a “knowledge graph” consists only of “triples” that are binary relations
knowledge graphs require global consistency within a “namespace”.
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor's characterisation of a competing technology.
assertions.reader_inference: Named-graph and quad-store practice in RDF systems is not discussed; the statement is a simplification.

assertions.value: The authors state that every axiom in the Cyc KB is either default true (generally true with exceptions) or monotonically true (true without exception), and that default axioms can be overridden by new knowledge.
quotes: Every axiom in the KB is either default true (i.e., generally true with exceptions) or monotonically true (i.e., true without exception).
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor's description of its own representation.

assertions.value: The authors state that deduction is sound but analogy, abduction and induction are not, and that since almost all the knowledge in Cyc's KB is default-true, even deduction in Cyc is not sound, so Cyc should give multiple answers with pro and con arguments rather than a single oracular answer.
quotes: Since almost all the knowledge in Cyc’s KB is just default-true, even deduction in Cyc is not sound
to have the system provide multiple answers, not just one
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 6 states this limit of its own reasoning in these words.
assertions.reader_inference: This is an author-stated limit: Cyc's conclusions are defeasible, not guaranteed.

assertions.value: The authors state that Cyc performs three types of reasoning during inference (deduction as its primary mode, induction, and abduction), that Cyc can also reason by analogy, and that induction is the only type of reasoning used by ML.
quotes: Cyc performs three types of reasoning during inference:
(This is Cyc’s primary mode of reasoning.)
(This is the only type of reasoning used by ML.)
assertions.certainty_reason: The claim about ML is a vendor generalisation about a competing technology.
assertions.reader_inference: The statement that induction is the only reasoning type in ML is a simplification; ML systems that use search, planning or symbolic components are not covered.

assertions.value: The authors state that Cyc holds two logically redundant representations of every assertion: the expressive Epistemological Level (EL) that is not very efficient, and the Heuristic Level (HL) that is very efficient to reason with; any EL statement can be translated into a logically equivalent HL statement.
quotes: Cyc developers have actually created two diﬀerent but logically redundant representations
Any CycL statement written in EL can be translated into a corresponding logically equivalent statement in the HL.
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor's description of its own architecture.

assertions.value: The authors state that Cyc becomes more efficient when the transitive closure of the genls relation is redundantly precomputed and stored, so that the axiom that dogs are partially tangible is concluded in one step.
quotes: even more eﬃcient if the transitive closure of the whole graph of that binary relation genls is—redundantly—precomputed and stored.
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor's description of its own optimisation; no timing is reported.

assertions.value: The authors state that 90% of the time Cyc calls on HL module agents to solve the current problem, 9% of the time it runs meta-level rules to decide whether to try a different tactic, and 1% of the time it runs meta-meta-level rules to decide whether to pick a whole different strategy.
quotes: 90% of the time, Cyc is calling on HL module agents
9% of the time, Cyc is sitting back and metaphorically puﬃng on its pipe
And 1% of the time, Cyc is running meta-meta-level rules
assertions.certainty_reason: Round percentages given without a measurement method.
assertions.reader_inference: The split is presented as a typical description; the paper reports no profiling data or workload.

assertions.value: The authors claim that meta- and meta-meta-level reasoning lets Cyc cope efficiently with amounts of data and numbers of rules that are four orders of magnitude larger than anyone else in symbolic AI ever tried to tackle.
quotes: amounts of data and numbers of rules that are four orders of magnitude larger than anyone else in symbolic AI ever tried to tackle.
assertions.certainty_reason: A comparative superlative with no comparison data.

assertions.value: The authors state a ladder of knowledge representation expressivity (propositional logic, a restricted subset of first order logic that includes knowledge graphs, quad- and triple-stores and RDF, full first order, second order, and higher-order logic), ordered from least to most expressive and from most to least efficient.
quotes: We have ordered them, here, from least to most expressive, and also from most to least eﬃcient:
Included here are knowledge graphs, quad- and triple-stores, and
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor's framing of the expressivity and efficiency trade-off.

assertions.value: The authors state that, when a Cyc application is deployed, typically over 99% of the knowledge that would need to be represented is already present in Cyc, and that when it is running, typically over 95% of the knowledge used in producing an answer and its justification was learned years earlier, on average about ten years earlier.
quotes: typically over 99% of the knowledge that would need to be represented, in order for the application to operate, is already present in Cyc.
typically over 95% of the knowledge that gets used in producing an answer and its justiﬁcation
assertions.certainty_reason: Typical-case percentages stated by the vendor without a measurement method or sample.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper does not say how many applications the percentages were taken from.

assertions.value: The authors report that a client-specific Cyc application in enterprise network security needed the Cyc KB expanded by a factor of .0001 (one ten-thousandth), because Cyc already had knowledge of information-bearing things.
quotes: a factor of .0001 (one ten-thousandth) because Cyc already had rich knowledge of the types of information-bearing things
assertions.certainty_reason: One unnamed client application, reported by the vendor without data.

assertions.value: The authors state that Cyc captures rules of thumb about how the world works, and that the rule that restricting flow in a fluid conduit increases pressure upstream has been used by Cyc to reason about oil pipelines, blood vessels, traffic arteries and drinking straws.
quotes: Restricting ﬂow in a ﬂuid conduit increases pressure upstream of the restriction.
has been used successfully by Cyc in applications where it had to reason about blockages in oil pipelines
assertions.certainty_reason: An anecdotal reuse example from the vendor.

assertions.value: The authors state that in a Cyc application for the Cleveland Clinic, a rule that a physical part generally cannot be removed twice helped disambiguate a query phrase about appendectomies, where the word and must mean or, and that a conduit-blockage rule first used for oil pipelines was reused for blood flow in arteries and veins.
quotes: “Once a physical part has been removed from an object, it generally can’t be removed again.”
the word “and ” must actually mean “or ”
assertions.certainty_reason: An anecdote from a vendor case; the application is cited to an AI Magazine article but not measured here.

assertions.value: The authors state that customizing Cyc for a client takes two phases: in Phase 1 Cycorp ontologists interview domain experts, often for as little as 4 or 5 hours, and in Phase 2 the client uses Cyc-generated web-based knowledge entry tools to maintain and extend the KB.
quotes: Cycorp ontologists spend some time (often as little as 4 or 5 hours) interviewing domain Subject Matter Experts
The client uses Cyc-generated knowledge entry tools to ﬁne-tune, maintain, and enhance the Cyc KB
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor's description of its own deployment process with an unverified effort figure.

assertions.value: The authors claim that the time and resources required to build an enterprise's (n + 1)th Cyc application decreases as n increases, which they call a knowledge network effect.
quotes: The time and resources required to build your enterprise’s (n + 1)th application decreases as n increases
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor's claim about customer cost curves; no data is given.

assertions.value: The authors state that Cyc does not import customer data into its Knowledge Base but accesses databases and web services in place through semantic knowledge source integration (SKSI), which they call virtual data-warehousing or data-laking, and that the data needs no migration.
quotes: Cyc does not do a wholesale import of the data into its Knowledge Base.
the customer data continues to live in customer databases, with no need for data migration.
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor's description of its own architecture.

assertions.value: The authors claim that Cyc approaches multi-database interaction as a linear mapping problem as opposed to a quadratic one, and so reduces the problem of integrating n structured data sources to a linear factor of n.
quotes: approach multi-database interactions as a linear mapping problem as opposed to a quadratic one
assertions.certainty_reason: A complexity claim without an argument or measurement in the paper.
assertions.reader_inference: The text layer prints the n squared formula garbled across lines; the quoted sentence holds the claim in words.

assertions.value: The authors state that once Cyc's ontology is aligned with the schema of a relational database, Cyc can automatically generate arbitrarily complex SQL queries to access any field in any row, and can query other data sources too.
quotes: Cyc is then able to automatically generate arbitrarily complex SQL queries
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor's description of its own capability.

assertions.value: The authors state that Cyc's knowledge base holds general rules rather than volatile facts, because directly encoding in the KB the stock price of each company on the New York Stock Exchange would be pointless as it would rapidly become stale; such data is consulted at the source in real time.
quotes: Directly encoding in the Cyc KB the stock price of each company on the New York Stock Exchange would be pointless
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor's design statement about its own platform.
assertions.reader_inference: This matches the Evidence Based DB rule that determinate or volatile facts are resolved, not stored; it is a design stance in the paper, not a tested result.

assertions.value: The authors report that a Cyc application for a global energy supermajor monitored real time oil production processes and alerted engineers to conditions of interest, and that it yielded fewer false positive alarms and fewer false negative missed conditions of interest, with pro and con arguments and English explanations for each alert.
quotes: The Cyc-enabled monitoring and alerting application yielded fewer false positive alarms and fewer false negative missed COIs.
assertions.certainty_reason: An unnamed client outcome reported by the vendor with no rates or baseline.
assertions.reader_inference: No false positive or false negative rate and no comparison system are reported.

assertions.value: The authors report that a Cyc application for a global pharmaceutical company generated plausible novel scenarios involving opioid fraud for one of the largest online pharmacy benefits management companies, and then identified possible cases of those in prescription data, finding previously unflagged bad doctors, bad patients and complicit local pharmacies.
quotes: Generating plausible novel scenarios involving opioid fraud, for one of the largest online pharmacy beneﬁts management companies
assertions.certainty_reason: An anecdotal client outcome reported by the vendor with no numbers.
assertions.reader_inference: This is a fraud-detection use of scenario generation plus data matching; no detection rates or comparison to statistical methods are reported.

assertions.value: The authors list a Cyc application for a global investment bank that monitors compliance with, and reports on, internal policies and external regulations.
quotes: Monitoring compliance with and reporting on internal policies and external regulations.
assertions.certainty_reason: A one-line description of an unnamed client application; no outcome is given.

assertions.value: The authors report that at the Cleveland Clinic, a short interactive query-articulation dialogue with Cyc cut the mean time from initial query to an answer deemed acceptable from two weeks to a few minutes.
quotes: cut the mean time from initial query to an answer deemed acceptable from two weeks
assertions.certainty_reason: A single-client outcome reported by the vendor in a footnote; the cited AI Magazine paper is a separate source.
assertions.reader_inference: The quote ends before the 2–5 minute figure; the figure appears in the next line of the text layer.

assertions.value: The paper quotes a testimonial attributed to the Global Personalization Lead at Accenture that Cyc's step-by-step English explanations of its reasoning let users trust the system.
quotes: The step-by-step English explanations of the reasoning behind Cyc’s recommendations enabled users to trust the system
assertions.certainty_reason: A customer testimonial selected and published by the vendor.

assertions.value: The authors list nine enterprise problem properties for which they say Cyc could be a uniquely good fit, including a need for transparent and auditable answers, disparate data sources, and a lack of data to train statistical AIs.
quotes: Getting the right answer is not enough, it needs to be transparent and fully auditable
Lack of data to train statistical AIs or analytics
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor's sales criteria, not tested.

assertions.value: The authors state that their clients tell them Cyc's pro and con reasoning helps keep them from falling into cognitive traps like confirmation bias, anchoring and group-think.
quotes: helps keep them from falling into cognitive traps like conﬁrmation bias, anchoring, and group-think.
assertions.certainty_reason: Second-hand client feedback reported by the vendor.

assertions.value: The authors state that there is no AI today that can automatically read and understand unrestricted text, that Cyc is used with entity and topic recognition that is not true natural language understanding, that there are already some successful stylized NLU applications powered by Cyc, and that full NLU is a longer path.
quotes: there is no AI today which can automatically read and understand unrestricted text!
It is a longer path to full NLU, but our internal Cycorp team is beating its milestones on the roadmap to this goal.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 9 states that Cyc does not yet offer full NLU; the roadmap sentence is a vendor claim.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper states that its own platform does not yet reach full natural language understanding.

assertions.value: The authors state that the lexicons and grammars are language-specific and comprise only about 2% of the content of the Cyc KB, and that the other 98% is language-independent; replacing the English lexicon with a German one lets Cyc produce German paraphrases of anything expressed in CycL.
quotes: comprise only about 2% of the content of the Cyc KB today; the other 98% is language-independent
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor's content breakdown with no counting method given.

assertions.value: The authors describe a three-step ML plus Cyc loop: neural nets and knowledge graphs statistically identify promising correlations, Cyc formulates causal explanations for them, and those chains yield independently testable predictions that are checked back against the data.
quotes: Right-brain neural nets and knowledge graphs are good for statistically identifying promising correlations
Left-brain AI (i.e., Cyc) can then think about those correlations in order to formulate possible explanations
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor's description of a hybrid workflow with its product.
assertions.reader_inference: This is a design for combining statistical correlation finding and symbolic explanation, relevant to hybrid use of ML and a knowledge base.

assertions.value: The authors report that, in applications with Cleveland Clinic and the National Library of Medicine, Cyc constructed plausible biochemical pathways to explain a genome wide association study correlation of a point mutation with early-life osteoporosis, and that the decades-old Framingham data could then confirm a mid-pathway physiological consequence, elevated levels of bioactive vitamin D.
quotes: Going back to the decades-old Framingham data can then conﬁrm this otherwise-insigniﬁcant mid-pathway physiological consequence
assertions.certainty_reason: A single anecdotal example reported by the vendor with no data in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that Cyc can be deployed in the cloud or on-site, runs on an ordinary Windows, Linux or macOS laptop, needs only 12GB RAM and approximately 20GB of disk space, is CPU-bound, and installs as a bundle of files or a containerized standalone package.
quotes: It needs only 12GB RAM and approximately 20GB of disk space.
Its performance is CPU-bound, so the better the processor, the better Cyc’s speed
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor's statement of its own product requirements.

assertions.value: The paper reports no experiment, benchmark, dataset or formal proof; every quantitative statement in it (knowledge base size, reuse percentages, inference engine counts, deployment figures) is a vendor description.
quotes: Cyc is a revolutionary AI platform with human reasoning, knowledge,
Trusted, Transparent, Actually Intelligent
assertions.certainty_reason: This is a reader's description of the document type, and the quotes only show its marketing framing.
assertions.reader_inference: The reader read all 22 numbered pages and found no experimental section, method or error rates; this entry is the reader's finding about the document, so treat every figure in it as vendor-reported.
